uncited: Unlike standard NeRF which only models appearance, this family lifts 2D observations into a consistent 3D representation, enabling tasks such as zero-shot segmentation, object manipulation, and view-dependent reflection modeling [12095-semantic-and-feature-branches.md, 12404-nerf-for-object-segmentation.md, 12072-nrff.md].

Children include [Multi-Space Neural Radiance Field (MS-NeRF)](11707-multi-space-neural-radiance-field-ms-nerf.md), [NRFF](12072-nrff.md), [Semantic and Feature Branches](12095-semantic-and-feature-branches.md), [NeRF for Object Segmentation](12404-nerf-for-object-segmentation.md), [Semantic-NeRF](14889-semantic-nerf.md), and [Augmented Features (Avg, Var, Color)](15000-augmented-features-avg-var-color.md).
**Parameters:** $H$: Predefined maximum number of solid objects the network predicts.
**Pitfall:** Variable number of objects and large non-occupied volumes.
Augment sampled features with variance from multiple views to describe occupancy.

**Formula:** Density and latent features are computed as: $\sigma(\mathbf{p}), \hat{\mathbf{h}}(\mathbf{p}) = \text{G-MLP}(\bar{V}(\mathbf{p}), \gamma(\mathbf{p}))$, where $\bar{V}(\mathbf{p})$ is ray features aggregated and augmented from multi-view features, and $\gamma(\mathbf{p})$ is position encoding.

The concept of feature fields generalizes the original NeRF formulation, which maps $(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d}) \rightarrow (\mathbf{c}, \sigma)$, to $(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d}) \rightarrow (\mathbf{f}, \mathbf{c}, \sigma)$ [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that feature fields generalize the original NeRF formulation from mapping (x, d) -> (c, σ) to (x, d) -> (f, c, σ). Source [S1] explicitly confirms this by stating 'feature fields generalize the NeRF formulation to predict arbitrary per-point feature signals rather than only color' and provides the formal extension from F_Θ(x, d) -> (c, σ) to F_Θ(x, d) -> (f, c, σ). The citation [S1, unofficial] correctly attributes this information to the provided source.

**Definition:** Sampling point features along the ray from multi-view image features instead of low-resolution volume features to address the need for high-resolution images in NeRF [S4].

The claim states that the method samples point features along the ray from multi-view image features instead of low-resolution volume features to address the need for high-resolution images in NeRF. Source [S4] explicitly confirms this in Section 3.2, stating that previous NeRFs sample from high-resolution 3D volumes, but this method uses a lower grid resolution for detection which causes aliasing. To mitigate this, they sample from higher resolution 2D image feature maps (160x120) instead of the low-resolution volume. The notes also confirm the specific PSNR improvement (20.51 vs 18.93) resulting from this approach.

**Definition:** Variance of color features describes occupancy: low variance implies occupied 3D location (Lambertian assumption), high variance implies free space (different appearances from different views) [S4].

The claim states that variance of color features describes occupancy, where low variance implies occupied 3D locations (based on the Lambertian assumption) and high variance implies free space. Source [S4] explicitly states: 'The variance of the color features is able to roughly describe the occupancy of the 3D field... If the 3D location p is occupied, the variance of the observed features should be low under the assumption that the scene only contains Lambertian surfaces. On the other hand, if the location is in free space, different appearances would be observed from different views, and therefore the variance of color features would be high.' This matches the claim exactly.
